preconditions.description: The number of queries q is between 1 and 10,000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 100 and 1 <= k <= (n * (n + 1)) // 2 for n, k in queries)
preconditions.description: For each query, n is between 1 and 100, and k is between 1 and n(n+1)/2.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i][0] == 'YES' if any(is_valid_permutation(n, k, perm) for perm in generate_permutations(n)) else output[i][0] == 'NO' for i, (n, k) in enumerate(queries))
postconditions.description: For each query, the output is 'YES' if there exists a permutation of numbers from 1 to n with beauty equal to k, otherwise 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output[i]) == 2 if output[i][0] == 'YES' else len(output[i]) == 1 for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', there is an additional line with n numbers representing the permutation. If the output is 'NO', there is no additional line.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= num <= n for num in output[i][1]) if output[i][0] == 'YES' else True for i, (n, _) in enumerate(queries))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', the permutation contains numbers from 1 to n.
